logp.method_description: The octanol-water partition coefficients (P) of 1, 2 and 3 were determined using a shake-flask method following the method reported by Hickey et al.6 with some minor modifications. Briefly water (25 mL) and n-octanol (25 mL) were shaken together using a laboratory vortex, for 48 h to allow saturation of both phases. Stock solutions of the three compounds (10 mM) were prepared in DMF and a 1 μL aliquot was added to a 2 ml 50:50 water:octanol mixture. The resultant biphasic solutions were mixed for 2 h at 220 rpm and 25 oC. The mixture was then centrifuged (3000 × g, 30 min) to separate the phases. 0.5 mL was removed carefully from each phase and evaporated to dryness. The solids were resuspended in 8.5 mL water, 0.5 mL concentrated HCl, 0.5 mL HNO3 and 0.5 mL H2O2, digested in a microwave (Milestone EthosEZ Microwave Digestion System) and analyzed by ICP-MS (Thermo iCAP Q ICP-MS). LogP was defined as the logarithm of the ratio of the concentrations of the complex in the organic and aqueous phases (LogP = Log {[Au(org)]/[Au(aq)]}; values reported are the means of at least three separate experiments).
